citation: MIP-9, section 7 (docs/mip/0009-group-conversation.md): Markdown is parsed in the core into paragraphs, lists, code blocks and runs that are emphasized, strong, code or links. CommonMark itself is pulldown-cmark's; the cases pin what Muster folds it into.
why: Agents write Markdown and the human reads it in the banner and the conversation, which every platform's shell draws from these blocks. What a message looks like is therefore decided here once, and a change to it shows up as a failing case rather than as a message that quietly reads differently on one platform.

cases.name: plain text is one paragraph of one run
cases.why: Most messages are a sentence. Anything more than one paragraph of one unstyled run would make the common case pay for the rare one.

cases.name: emphasis, strong and inline code are runs of their own
cases.why: The three inline styles a message uses most. Each is its own run so a shell draws it with nothing more than a style per run.

cases.name: nested styles combine on one run
cases.why: Bold inside italics is both, not whichever opened last. A run carries every style that applies to it.

cases.name: a link carries its destination on its text
cases.why: A link is drawn as its words, which the shell makes something to click. The destination travels on the run so the shell need not parse anything.

cases.name: a soft break is a space and a hard break is a newline
cases.why: Agents wrap their source at a width the reader's view does not share, so a single newline must not break the line. Two trailing spaces or a backslash is the writer asking for a break, and gets one.

cases.name: paragraphs are separate blocks
cases.why: A blank line starts a new paragraph, which a shell spaces apart.

cases.name: a bulleted list holds each item's blocks
cases.why: A tight list's items have no paragraph around their text in CommonMark's events; the core still gives each item a paragraph, so a shell draws tight and loose lists alike.

cases.name: a numbered list keeps the number it starts at
cases.why: An agent continuing a list from an earlier message starts it at 4, and the human reads the numbers as references.

cases.name: a nested list sits inside its item
cases.why: Plans arrive as nested lists. The inner list belongs to the item above it, after that item's text.

cases.name: a fenced code block keeps its language and its lines
cases.why: Commands and diffs are pasted as fenced blocks, and must arrive exactly as written: no styling inside, no trailing newline the shell would draw as an empty line.

cases.name: an indented code block names no language
cases.why: CommonMark's other code block has no info string, so its language is empty rather than absent.

cases.name: markdown inside a code block stays text
cases.why: A code block is literal; asterisks in a shell glob are not emphasis.

cases.name: a heading is a strong paragraph
cases.why: A message has no outline to navigate, so a heading only needs to stand out, which strong does in every toolkit without the tree growing a block a shell must size.

cases.name: a quote is the blocks inside it
cases.why: Agents quote what they are answering; the words matter and the indent does not, so a quote folds into its own blocks rather than adding a block kind.

given.markdown:
> you said this

and I say that

cases.name: HTML is shown as the text it was written as
cases.why: Nothing renders HTML, so a tag the agent typed stays visible rather than vanishing along with whatever it wrapped.

cases.name: an image is its alt text, linked to the image
cases.why: A banner draws no images; the description and where to find it are what is left.

cases.name: a rule separates paragraphs and draws nothing
cases.why: A thematic break between two paragraphs leaves two paragraphs; it is not text.

cases.name: an empty message has no blocks
cases.why: Nothing to draw is an empty list, not a paragraph holding an empty run.

cases.name: the leading lines of a short message are all of it
cases.why: A banner shows a message's first lines; one that fits says nothing was cut, so no Show all is offered.

cases.name: the leading lines stop inside a paragraph at a hard break
cases.why: A line is what the source shows on one line, so a paragraph of hard-broken lines is cut between them.

cases.name: the leading lines count list items and code lines
cases.why: A list takes a line per item and a code block a line per line, so a banner holding a plan or a command shows its start and says the rest was cut.
